title: Honeycomb with capped and honey-filled cells
purpose: Generate tileable PBR maps of honeycomb: hexagonal wax cells with rounded walls, empty tubes, glossy honey that climbs the walls and domed wax caps in patches, from new white comb to dark brood comb. Use for beehives, honey props, food scenes, nature close-ups and sci-fi hex surfaces.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python honeycomb_comb.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: cells
parameters.meaning: Cells across the tile; the row count is the even number that keeps the hexagons near regular.

parameters.name: wall
parameters.meaning: Wax wall thickness as a share of the cell width.

parameters.name: capped
parameters.meaning: Share of cells sealed with a wax cap.

parameters.name: honey
parameters.meaning: Share of open cells holding honey; the rest are empty.

parameters.name: irregularity
parameters.meaning: How unevenly the cells are built: jitter of the cell centres.

parameters.name: age
parameters.meaning: Darkening of the wax with use: 0 new white comb, 1 old dark brood comb.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Golden comb with patches of capped cells among cells full of honey.

presets.name: fresh_white
presets.description: New white comb, mostly empty, with thin clean walls.

presets.name: brood_comb
presets.description: Dark old brood comb with brown domed caps.

presets.name: brimming_honey
presets.description: Large open cells brimming with amber honey.

limits: Cells are seen face-on as a height field: the depth of an empty cell is a short drop to a dark floor, not a modelled tube, and honey is an opaque glossy surface with no translucency or refraction. Larvae, pollen, bees and broken comb are out of scope. Capped and open cells gather by smooth noise rather than by colony behaviour. The hexagons come from a lattice made near-regular for the tile, so very low cell counts squash them slightly. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate.
technique_references: Worley cells of a jittered hexagonal lattice on the torus
Wax walls from the distance to the cell border
Domed caps from the distance to the cell centre
Noise field sampled per cell for capped patches
Height to tangent-space normal by central differences
